implemented_invariants: session_id, agent_id, task_id, turn_id, causal_id and generation are explicit typed fields
generation accepts only a true non-negative integer and rejects bool/coerced values
missing, empty, whitespace-padded, control-character and unexpected identity fields fail closed
canonical JSON is deterministic by sorted keys and compact separators
derived causal steps require a caller-supplied new causal_id and record parent_causal_id explicitly
transport/admission fields are not silently admitted into the causal identity envelope
no identifier or generation is invented from wall-clock time, process state or current working directory

local_test.note: The connector-visible committed source and tests were inspected after commit. The execution container could not clone github.com due DNS resolution failure, so the local run is not represented as a byte-exact Git checkout replay or VPS runtime receipt.

negative_evidence.detail: The first local test harness used importlib.util.exec_module without registering the module in sys.modules; Python 3.13 dataclass processing failed before product tests. The harness was corrected to normal sys.path/import semantics and 7/7 tests then passed.
Independent git clone of the canonical repository from the execution container failed because github.com DNS could not be resolved.

counterhypothesis: A clean causal identity type alone does not prove end-to-end causal closure. Runtime writers/readers may still diverge, omit fields, reuse stale generations or bind effects to the wrong identity unless later UnifiedDB, Typed Entry, telemetry and effect-path integration enforce this envelope.
next_exact_action: Bind CausalIdentity into the F2-WP-100 UnifiedDB/coordination layer and causal telemetry writer once their current interfaces stabilize, then execute an exact-repository integration test that proves event -> persisted identity -> telemetry lineage without field loss or generation drift.
